items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: I had not worked with Charlie Shavers at the time but we knew Charlie pretty well and met him on Broadway.

ctx.x: Your first experience in bebop, where did that take place? Back in New York?

Yeah. Back in New York. I had not worked with Charlie Shavers at the time but we knew Charlie pretty well and met him on Broadway. When I say “we,” Dodo Marmarosa, who was quite a piano player. I would say at fourteen years old he was one of the best in the world, jazz piano player, who also recorded with Bird and was on all of the bands that I’ve played with including Tommy Dorsey. He was with Artie Shaw as well. Dodo Marmarosa. Artie loved his playing. But he and I ran into Charlie Shavers. And Charlie Shavers…
It takes an awful lot of facility to pull that off.

items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Now, was it when you were in the Dorsey band, you and Charlie Shavers... Yeah, it was, I think Charlie Shavers came, we ran into on Broadway sometime... We had sometime off, so we went to hear bird.

ctx.x: Now, was it when you were in the Dorsey band, you and Charlie Shavers, didn’t you kind of discover bebop around then? Didn’t you hear Charlie Parker for the first time with Charlie Shavers?

Yeah, it was, I think Charlie Shavers came, we ran into on Broadway sometime, and he said. “I heard this guy playing saxophone up in Harlem.” And he said, “I don’t know what he’s doing but it’s unbelievable. It’s fantastic stuff. He said, “I’m going to go up and listen to him the next couple of nights.” Or whatever it was. We had sometime off, so we went to hear bird. Strange, he was playing with a borrowed
saxophone, wasn’t even his. And he played this strange jazz, you know, for us it was kind of strange.
